summary: Forest Service lookout site in Augusta County, VA, registered 2015. The tower lies on the ground and a partly standing cabin is nearby.

facts.design: Unclear: either an Aeromotor windmill tower or a CAA aircraft beacon tower, with a unique 6 by 6 foot cab
facts.status_note: The tower lies on the ground; a partly standing lookout cabin is nearby.

events.note: Registered June 9, 2015, on the nomination of Renick Proffitt

evidence.supports: tower remains lie on the ground
evidence.quote: The remains of the Hardscrabble Knob fire tower now lie on the ground.
A partially standing cabin previously used by lookouts is nearby.

evidence.supports: built and used by the Forest Service
evidence.quote: It was built and used by the U.S. Forest Service.

evidence.supports: design is either a windmill tower or a CAA beacon tower with a 6x6 cab
evidence.quote: either an Aeromotor windmill tower or a CAA aircraft beacon tower that was fitted with a unique 6'x6' cab

evidence.supports: only known example of this design
evidence.quote: Hardscrabble Knob is the only known example of a fire tower of this design.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts labels the site Ruins

notes_for_editor: No build year, staffing, fire or removal record in either source. The register gives the design as either/or, so the design fact is marked unclear. The register credits the photo to Renick Proffitt; no image URL was captured. A Wikipedia page for Hardscrabble Knob returned 404. The Forest Lookouts page adds only county, forest and the status Ruins.
